Of all the tickets printed for "50X The Cash", only a small slice are still unsold. The game is in the last part of its run, with one of six top prizes unclaimed. In every scratcher, either the tickets or the prizes run out first. The rest of this page shows the details.

The table below shows the full count for "50X The Cash", with every prize level included.
981.headline: How much has sold

985.body:
The key fact about "MAX-A-MILLION" is how its thirteen prize levels are built. The prize money leans toward many smaller prizes. Games built like this pay out often, in small amounts. Prize counts change daily, but this design does not.

If "MAX-A-MILLION" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
985.headline: How prizes are split

988.body:
The prize money on "Emerald 10's" leans toward many smaller prizes. It is spread over eleven prize levels, from wins equal to the ticket price up to $1 million. Games built like this pay out often, in small amounts. That design never changes, and it is the part you choose.

Tomorrow's count on "Emerald 10's" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
988.headline: Same price, different prizes

990.body:
"LADY LUCK" has two of four top prizes left and is well into its run. About three-quarters of the tickets are already sold. As a game goes on, the same prizes are spread across fewer tickets. Right now, the top prizes are being claimed more slowly than the tickets are selling, which is a good sign.

Every line of LADY LUCK's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
990.headline: How far along this game is

992.body:
The top prize count on "$2 MILLION VAULT" has not moved since we started watching it. The game still has one of three top prizes unclaimed. Smaller prizes keep getting claimed as tickets sell. The same top prizes are now among fewer tickets.

Everything here about "$2 MILLION VAULT" comes from official North Carolina lottery numbers, current through October 25.
992.headline: No top prize claimed lately

993.body:
About three-quarters of the tickets for "$5,000 Triple Play" are sold. The top prize count has held, with three of six still unclaimed. The number of tickets printed is fixed, so that is a plain good sign.

The numbers for "$5,000 Triple Play" will change a little by tomorrow, and this page will change with them.
993.headline: Top prizes have lasted so far

994.body:
"$25,000 Triple Play" has one of four top prizes left and is in the second half of its run. About three-quarters of the tickets are already sold. As a game goes on, the same prizes are spread across fewer tickets. Right now, tickets and top prizes are running out at about the same rate.

Tomorrow's count on "$25,000 Triple Play" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
994.headline: How far along this game is

995.body:
"$200,000 Triple Play" is well into its run, with about a quarter of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, a larger share of the top prizes is left than of the tickets, which is a good sign.

Today's free summary of "$200,000 Triple Play" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.
995.headline: Early stage or late

996.body:
About two-thirds of the tickets for "$1,000,000 Triple Play" are sold. The top prize count has held, with four of five still unclaimed. The number of tickets printed is fixed, so that is a plain good sign.

Every line of $1,000,000 Triple Play's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
996.headline: Good news: no big claims
